newsitem.title: CROATIA: Zagrebacka breaks high on active Croatian bourse.
newsitem.headline: Zagrebacka breaks high on active Croatian bourse.

text.p: Zagrebacka Banka broke through its all-time high on the Zagreb bourse on Thursday, leading a pack of gainers in an active market and brokers foresaw only mild changes by the end of the week.
Drugs concern Pliva also traded well and made new gains and dealers said there was more yet to come.

"Zagrebacka and Pliva which accounted for more than 80 percent of the trade, boosted liquidity and we can expect such solid liquidity to continue," Hrvoje Bujanovic of Investment Bank Austria told Reuters.
"Zagrebacka's rise yesterday was purely based on the strong dollar, but today it was a quality jump decided by the market makers in London," said Bujanovic.
He said growth might continue this week, but a steeper rise could come in September when the bank is expected to offer cheaper capital, after getting a 400 million mark syndicated loan last month.

Fully-listed Zagrebacka was the day's most active stock, closing up 99.88 kuna or 4.5 percent. It closed at 2,305.12 kuna after trading in a 2,200-2,335 kuna range. Its previous all-time high was reached in April 2,300.
Its Global Depository Receipts (GDRs), trading in U.S. dollars in London, fetched $36.125, up from $34.875 at the open.
Pliva rose 10.9 kuna or 2.1 percent to 536 kuna on volume of 4.131. "I believe Pliva could see some more gains as well," said Bujanovic.
Eight of 16 active issues rose, four fell and four were flat. Volume halved to 14,676 units and turnover slid to 13.9 from 16.9 million kuna on Wednesday.
Varazdinska Banka which also trades in the top bracket of the bourse stood its ground at 210 kuna and sold 1,043 shares.

Food processor Podravka added three kuna to 252 on volume of 1,917. Bigger packages indicated significant investors were still at work, but traders said stagnation and smaller corrections were on the cards.
Five active hoteliers traded mixed on a smaller scale and analysts pointed out Istraturist, which added four kuna to 174, as the only exception. It sold 500 shares.
"All tourist stocks are now in a state of correction," one trader said, but added good revenue from the current holiday season might lift them up later in August.
Dalmatinska Banka led decliners and lost 27 kuna or 8.2 percent to 303 on volume of 300 shares.
